hints: How many units can you add before reaching ten?
body.solution_sketch: Count on from ${a}$ by ${b}$; when the sum crosses ten, fill ten first and add the remaining units.

hints: How many units can you add before reaching ten?
body.solution_sketch: Count on from ${a}$ by ${b}$; when the sum crosses ten, fill ten first and add the remaining units.

hints: Where do you land when you count back the requested units?
body.solution_sketch: Count back ${b}$ units from ${a}$. If you pass ten, subtract down to ten before taking away the remaining units.

hints: Where do you land when you count back the requested units?
body.solution_sketch: Count back ${b}$ units from ${a}$. If you pass ten, subtract down to ten before taking away the remaining units.

hints: Which multiplication fact gives the total of these equal groups?
body.solution_sketch: Count ${a}$ equal groups of ${b}$ by repeated addition.

hints: Which multiplication fact gives the total of these equal groups?
body.solution_sketch: Count ${a}$ equal groups of ${b}$ by repeated addition.

hints: What must multiply the known factor to make the product?
body.solution_sketch: Find the multiplication fact with factor ${b}$ and product ${a}$; its other factor is the quotient.

hints: What must multiply the known factor to make the product?
body.solution_sketch: Find the multiplication fact with factor ${b}$ and product ${a}$; its other factor is the quotient.

hints: Which columns need an exchange into the next place?
body.solution_sketch: Align place values for two-digit addition with a units carry. Add each column from the units leftward; exchange each ten units in a column for one unit in the next column.

hints: Which columns need an exchange into the next place?
body.solution_sketch: Align place values for units and tens carries. Add each column from the units leftward; exchange each ten units in a column for one unit in the next column.

hints: Which columns need an exchange into the next place?
body.solution_sketch: Align place values for multiple carries in four-digit addition. Add each column from the units leftward; exchange each ten units in a column for one unit in the next column.

hints: What is the units-column total when you include all three addends?
body.solution_sketch: Align all three addends by place value. Add their units first, carry any full tens, then add the tens and the carried amount.

hints: Which column needs an exchange, and how can addition check your difference?
body.solution_sketch: Subtract by place value with one borrow. Exchange a higher-place unit when needed; then add the difference to ${b}$ to recover ${a}$.
body.statement: Compute ${a} - {b}$ and check the difference by addition.

hints: Which column needs an exchange, and how can addition check your difference?
body.solution_sketch: Subtract by place value with borrowing between nonzero places. Exchange a higher-place unit when needed; then add the difference to ${b}$ to recover ${a}$.
body.statement: Compute ${a} - {b}$ and check the difference by addition.

hints: Which column needs an exchange, and how can addition check your difference?
body.solution_sketch: Subtract by place value with an addition check. Exchange a higher-place unit when needed; then add the difference to ${b}$ to recover ${a}$.
body.statement: Compute ${a} - {b}$ and check the difference by addition.

hints: How can you pass an exchange across the zero columns?
body.solution_sketch: Exchange one thousand for hundreds, one of those hundreds for tens, and one ten for units. Subtract the units, tens and hundreds of ${a}$ from the regrouped places.

hints: What subtotal do you need before performing the subtraction?
body.solution_sketch: Add the first two quantities by place value; subtract the final quantity from that subtotal.

hints: What operation combines the original supply and the new tickets?
body.solution_sketch: Add the newly printed tickets to the original supply.
body.statement: A museum had ${a}$ tickets and printed $286$ more. How many tickets does it have now?

hints: Which change decreases the stock, and which change increases it?
body.solution_sketch: Subtract the sold notebooks from the initial stock, then add the delivery to the remaining stock.
body.statement: A shop had ${a}$ notebooks, sold $86$, then received $47$ more. How many notebooks remain?

hints: How does the stated difference connect the two totals?
body.solution_sketch: Ava's total includes Leo's total and the extra cards. Subtract the extra cards to find Leo's total.
body.statement: Ava has ${a}$ cards, which is $57$ more than Leo has. How many cards does Leo have?

hints: What multiplication counts every seat once?
body.solution_sketch: Multiply the number of equal rows by the seats in each row.
body.statement: A hall has ${a}$ rows with $17$ seats in each row. How many seats are there?

hints: How many groups of the box size make the total?
body.solution_sketch: Divide the total number of pencils by the number in one box. Multiply the quotient by the box size to check the total.
body.statement: ${a}$ pencils are packed with $7$ pencils in each box. How many boxes are filled?

hints: Can any pupil left after filling the full minibuses travel without another vehicle?
body.solution_sketch: Divide pupils by seats per minibus. When pupils remain, another minibus is required even if it is partly empty.
body.statement: ${a}$ pupils need transport. Each minibus has $18$ seats. How many minibuses are needed for everyone?

hints: Does a partly filled bag count as a full bag?
body.solution_sketch: Count complete groups of the bag size. Set aside leftover oranges because they cannot fill another bag.
body.statement: ${a}$ oranges are packed in bags holding $7$ oranges each. How many full bags can be packed?

hints: Which digit occupies the tens column?
body.solution_sketch: Read the tens digit and multiply its face value by ten.
body.statement: What is the value of the tens digit in ${a}$?

hints: What is the place value of the fourth digit from the right?
body.solution_sketch: Locate the thousands digit, including when other places hold zero, and multiply that digit by one thousand.
body.statement: What is the value of the thousands digit in ${a}$?

hints: Does the units digit put the number below or at least halfway to the next ten?
body.solution_sketch: Look at the units digit. Keep the tens digit for units below five; otherwise increase the tens digit. Replace the units digit with zero.

hints: Is the number below, at, or above the halfway point?
body.solution_sketch: Locate the two neighboring thousands. Compare the number with their midpoint; at the midpoint round to the higher thousand.

hints: Which place will each digit occupy after multiplying by one hundred?
body.solution_sketch: Multiplication by one hundred moves each digit two place-value columns to the left. Fill empty positions with zero.

hints: How do the units product and tens product combine?
body.solution_sketch: Multiply the units by the single-digit factor, carry the tens, then multiply the tens and add the carried amount.

hints: How will you keep the internal zero's column in the calculation?
body.solution_sketch: Work from units to hundreds, multiplying each place by the one-digit factor and carrying into the next place.

hints: What partial products come from splitting the second factor into tens and units?
body.solution_sketch: Find the partial products for the units and tens of the second factor. Align their place values and add.

hints: Which partial product represents multiplication by tens?
body.solution_sketch: Multiply the three-digit factor by each place of the two-digit factor; shift the tens partial product one place before adding.

hints: How can the distributive property break this into two easier products?
body.solution_sketch: Split the second factor into forty and three. Add the product with forty to the product with three, then compare with a rounded estimate.

hints: What table fact remains after factoring out a ten from each operand?
body.solution_sketch: Multiply the nonzero tens digits using the multiplication table. Each factor contributes a factor of ten, so scale that product by one hundred.

hints: How does increasing the first factor by one change the product?
body.solution_sketch: Replace the first factor by the next multiple of ten, multiply, then subtract one group of the second factor.

hints: After subtracting each partial product, which digit should you bring down next?
body.solution_sketch: Divide from the highest place, multiply the quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, and bring down the next digit. Check by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.

hints: After subtracting each partial product, which digit should you bring down next?
body.solution_sketch: Divide from the highest place, multiply the quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, and bring down the next digit. Check by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.

hints: After subtracting each partial product, which digit should you bring down next?
body.solution_sketch: Divide from the highest place, multiply the quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, and bring down the next digit. Check by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.

hints: After subtracting each partial product, which digit should you bring down next?
body.solution_sketch: Divide from the highest place, multiply the quotient digit by the divisor, subtract, and bring down the next digit. Check by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.

hints: How many equal factors does a square contain?
body.solution_sketch: A square is the product of two equal factors. Multiply the base by itself.

hints: What value does each power represent?
body.solution_sketch: Compute the square and cube by repeated multiplication, then compare their numerical values.
body.statement: Which value is larger: ${a}^{{2}}$ or ${b}^{{3}}$? Give its numerical value.

hints: Which sum is grouped before the multiplication?
body.solution_sketch: Add the two numbers inside the parentheses first, then multiply that subtotal by the outside factor.

hints: How much does the grouped subtraction tell you to remove?
body.solution_sketch: Subtract inside the parentheses to find the amount being removed. Subtract that entire amount from the leading number.

hints: Which words tell you to group an addition?
body.solution_sketch: The phrase 'the sum' groups the addition. Find that sum before multiplying it by the final factor.
body.statement: Evaluate: multiply the sum of ${a}$ and $6$ by $5$.

hints: Which operation must be completed before adding?
body.solution_sketch: Find the product first because multiplication takes precedence over addition; then add the leading number.

hints: What must you evaluate before forming the product?
body.solution_sketch: Square the base, multiply that square by the following factor, then add the leading number.

hints: What two values must be ready before the final subtraction?
body.solution_sketch: Evaluate the grouped sum and square it. Compute the separate product, then subtract that product from the square.

hints: Which neighboring ten is closest to each addend?
body.solution_sketch: Round each addend independently to its nearest ten using the units digit. Add the rounded numbers to obtain the estimate.
body.statement: Estimate ${a} + 36$ by rounding each number to the nearest ten.

hints: How can the rounded factors make multiplication easier?
body.solution_sketch: Round each factor to the nearest ten, then multiply the rounded factors using their tens digits and place values.
body.statement: Estimate ${a} \times 28$ by rounding each factor to the nearest ten.

hints: On which side of the midpoint between the two choices does the sum lie?
body.solution_sketch: The midpoint of the two offered totals is six hundred fifty. Compare the sum with that midpoint to select the closer offered total.
body.statement: Without calculating exactly, is ${a} + 298$ closer to $600$ or $700$?

hints: At which place do the two numbers first differ?
body.solution_sketch: Compare digit counts, then compare matching places from left to right. The first unequal digit determines the larger number.

hints: Which numbers share a hundreds digit and need a closer comparison?
body.solution_sketch: Compare the hundreds digits first and then tens and units when tied. Place the smallest first and the largest last.

hints: Which divisors appear in both factor lists?
body.solution_sketch: List factor pairs for each number, identify the factors shared by both lists, and select the largest shared factor.

hints: Which divisors appear in both factor lists?

hints: Which divisors appear in both factor lists?
body.solution_sketch: List factor pairs for each number, identify the factors shared by both lists, and select the largest shared factor.

hints: Where do the two lists of multiples first meet?
body.solution_sketch: List positive multiples of both numbers until a value appears in both lists; choose the first shared value.

hints: Does the smaller number divide the larger, or do they share no factor greater than unity?
body.solution_sketch: Check whether the smaller number divides the larger. If so, the larger is the LCM. Otherwise these pairs are relatively prime, so multiply the two inputs.

hints: What is the first positive value divisible by all three inputs?
body.solution_sketch: Find a common multiple of the first two numbers, then take the least common multiple of that value and the third number.

hints: Which prime powers are present in both factorizations?
body.solution_sketch: Factor both inputs into primes. For each prime shared by the inputs, keep its smaller exponent; multiply those shared prime powers.
body.statement: Find the GCF of ${a}$ and $84$ using prime factorization.

hints: Which prime powers are needed to make a multiple of both inputs?
body.solution_sketch: Factor both inputs into primes. Keep the larger exponent of every prime that occurs in either input, then multiply those prime powers.
body.statement: Find the LCM of ${a}$ and $36$ using prime factorization.

hints: What kind of common multiple gives the next shared event?
body.solution_sketch: The next shared ringing time must be a positive multiple of both intervals. Select their least common multiple.
body.statement: Two bells ring together now. One rings every ${a}$ minutes and the other every $18$ minutes. In how many minutes will they next ring together?

hints: Which smaller primes must you test to rule out a composite candidate?
body.solution_sketch: Check successive integers above the given number. For each candidate, test divisibility by primes up to its square root. Stop at the first candidate with no such divisor.
body.statement: What is the smallest prime greater than ${a}$?

hints: Can you express either candidate as a product of two equal whole numbers?
body.solution_sketch: Compare each candidate with the products of a whole number multiplied by itself. Select the candidate that equals one of these products.
body.statement: Exactly one of ${a}$ and ${b}$ is a perfect square. Which number is it?
